title: Physics on arXiv — Friday, 2 October 2026: 9 notable new papers
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper shortlist, not a popularity ranking; citation evidence is limited for the newly announced batch, and archive coverage is a front-page sample rather than an exhaustive crawl.

sections.title: Search for dark matter produced in association with a low-multiplicity jet in proton-proton collisions at √s = 13 TeV
sections.abstract: CMS reports the first LHC search using a low-multiplicity jet signature, finding no excess and setting dark-matter production limits with 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New collaboration search channel described as the first of its kind at the LHC; based on 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data and submitted to Physical Review D.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe no excess and exclude mediator masses up to 4.25 TeV for a dark-matter mass near 150 GeV in the stated simplified models.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; CMS 13 TeV proton-proton collision data, 138 fb⁻¹, with supervised machine learning for sensitivity
sections.unique_caveat: Limits are conditional on the simplified vector/axial-vector mediator models; the search finds no dark-matter signal.

sections.title: Search for charged-lepton-flavour violating eμtq interactions at √s = 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
sections.abstract: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV ATLAS data, the collaboration finds no significant deviation from the Standard Model and sets 95% confidence limits on six effective-field-theory coefficients and related top-decay branching fractions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large-collaboration result using the stated 140 fb⁻¹ sample, with explicit EFT constraints, submitted to JHEP.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report branching-ratio upper bounds spanning 6 × 10⁻⁹ to 2.7 × 10⁻⁷ for the specified eμu/eμc top-decay couplings.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ATLAS proton-proton collision data at the LHC, interpreted in an effective field theory framework
sections.unique_caveat: No signal is observed; the quoted limits depend on the EFT interpretation and the analyzed 13 TeV dataset.

sections.title: A New Framework for Modeling Solar Flares from MHD to Kinetic Processes
sections.abstract: The authors link three specialized models to simulate flare initiation, particle acceleration and transport, atmospheric heating, and emission, reporting simulated white-light emission heights consistent with observations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Integrated ARMS–kglobal–RADYN+FP pipeline, accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal, with modeled emission heights compared to observations.
sections.claimed_result: The paper demonstrates a detailed simulation tracking nonthermal electrons and protons in the same reconnected loop and produces white-light emission heights consistent with observations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; coupled 2.5D MHD, kinetic particle-acceleration, and radiative-hydrodynamic simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe this as a first step toward a fully 3D framework; the result is a model-to-observation consistency, not a new observation.

sections.title: Polynomial-time classical and quantum simulation of quantum impurity models
sections.abstract: The authors prove polynomial-time classical algorithms for static impurity-model properties, while showing that nonequilibrium Green’s functions capture quantum-computational power.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in quantum physics, strongly correlated electrons, computational complexity, algorithms, and chemical physics; gives explicit polynomial-time bounds for equilibrium quantities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors improve ground-state-energy estimation from quasipolynomial to polynomial time and establish polynomial-time guarantees for thermal equilibrium; they show dynamical simulation can encode the full power of quantum computation.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; computational-complexity results and algorithms for impurity models
sections.unique_caveat: These are complexity-theoretic results for the stated impurity-model setting; they do not establish practical runtime advantages on a particular device.

sections.title: Programmable nonlinearity within nanophotonic waveguides
sections.abstract: By optically programming χ² patterns in waveguides after fabrication, the authors demonstrate reconfigurable quasi-phase matching, in-situ optimization, and device diagnostics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Experimental demonstration of post-fabrication reconfiguration in about one second and several concrete functions, including phase-mismatch compensation and on-chip diagnostics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use structured illumination and photoconductive electrodes to program effective χ² patterns for spectral, modal, and polarization control of three-wave mixing.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; nonlinear nanophotonic waveguides with optically induced nonlinearity and closed-loop optimization
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract demonstrates the method in specific waveguide structures; broader performance and scalable cascaded systems remain prospective.

sections.title: Thermal axion production in QCD from the lattice
sections.abstract: The authors show that weighted light-cone integrals relevant to thermal axion production can be computed from Euclidean lattice QCD without analytic continuation, and test feasibility in pure-glue QCD.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New lattice-based route to a key early-Universe production quantity that avoids analytic continuation; abstract reports feasibility at 1.5 T_c.
sections.claimed_result: In pure-glue QCD at 1.5 T_c, the authors find it feasible to extract at least one, and possibly two, finite weighted momentum integrals of the production rate.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Euclidean lattice-QCD calculations in pure-glue QCD
sections.unique_caveat: The feasibility study is in pure-glue QCD; application to full QCD near and above the crossover is a prospective next step, not a result already obtained.

sections.title: Thin-capping layer epitaxial quantum dots for near-field quantum photonics
sections.abstract: Optical characterization of InAs/GaAs quantum dots with thinner capping layers finds up to five-times-narrower emission linewidths than previously reported while preserving excitonic lifetimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed materials/optics/quantum-photonics experiment with quantitative linewidth comparison across three capping thicknesses.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that 10 nm and 20 nm capped dots retain optical quality, including unperturbed excitonic lifetimes, while placing emitters closer to surfaces for near-field coupling.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; epitaxial InAs/GaAs quantum-dot growth and optical characterization
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes optical properties for the tested structures; a fully integrated near-field photonic-device demonstration is not reported there.

sections.title: Hyperbolic lattices with mass disorder: Phases and phase transitions
sections.abstract: Numerical tight-binding calculations show how mass disorder changes phases and drives metal–insulator transitions on three specified hyperbolic lattices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Spans three condensed-matter categories and reports multiple disorder-driven transitions with computed critical exponents.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the hyperbolic Dirac liquid survives weak mass disorder, then undergoes semimetal-to-metal and, at stronger disorder, Anderson metal-to-insulator transitions; the other two lattice models show only the latter transition.
sections.evidence_type: computational; tight-binding models on {10,3}, {8,3}, and {8,4} hyperbolic lattices, analyzed with the kernel polynomial method
sections.unique_caveat: Results are numerical for the specified lattice geometries, nearest-neighbor models, and disorder scheme; they are not an experimental observation.

sections.title: Analytic Metric for Rotating Black Holes in Higher-Derivative Gravity
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an analytic metric-reconstruction method and construct a rotating black-hole solution in parity-even cubic gravity at linear order in the coupling.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Claims a new analytic spinning solution without spin or weak-field expansions and reports validation against field equations and independent horizon predictions.
sections.claimed_result: In parity-even cubic gravity, the authors construct an analytic rotating black-hole metric at linear order in the coupling and reproduce independent analytic predictions for horizon properties.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; analytic metric reconstruction and field-equation validation
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated solution is for one modified-gravity theory and is linear in its coupling; the abstract does not establish a general metric for arbitrary higher-derivative theories.
